newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds held hostage to U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds held hostage to U.S. data.

text.p: *Australian bond yields finished above the day's lows as the market succumbed to quieter session ahead of the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report for January later today.
*The data is seen rising 237,000 vs 262,000 in December.
Australian bond yields finished above the day's lows as the market succumbed to a quieter session ahead of the key U.S. labour force for January.

U.S. non-farm payrolls are seen rising 237,000 on average after the 262,000 leap in December, but a figure above 275,000 and at the top of the expected range, could prompt a large sell-off in U.S. Treasuries, according to U.S. analysts.

With local market already blistering from Thursday's steep data-led sell-off, traders were content to sit and wait for the U.S. jobs result, rather than follow-though the technical rebound seen in after hours trading.
Thursday's latest data on wages, which saw growth at the top end of expectations, saw a marked sell-off as the market unwound the chances of an imminent easing in monetary policy.

However, a Reuters poll of economists taken today still gave a 45 percent chance of a further rate cut in the current cycle as yesterday's data did not suggest an imminent inflation blowout, and the inflation and wages outlook could still accommodate another easing.
But the two main keys to a cut would be the performance of the real economy in the coming months, and the outcome of the unions' 'living wage' claim, analysts added.

Traders said the local offshore demand included buying against Canadian debt after Thursday's near 1/4 point spread blow-out. The New Zealand debt market returned from Thursday's local holiday weaker as it adjusted to the higher yield levels of offshore markets in its absence.
